body.statement: Can the exact pilot-localized multinomial inversion handle be completed so that \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}P\{(\underline\theta_d(p),\overline\theta_d(p))_{d\in\mathcal D}\in\mathcal I_{N,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\) for every \(N\), including empty arms, zero cells, and tied active facets, while at each fixed positive-support law with one separated active contrast and positive contrast variance the corresponding scalar side of \(\mathcal I_{N,1-\alpha}\) is asymptotically equivalent to the semiparametrically efficient Wald interval?
body.justification: Identification without boundary-valid uncertainty quantification is inadequate for sparse multi-arm ordinal trials.
body.gap: ChoRussell2024 perturbs LPs for uniform validity and FangSantos2019 simulates directional derivatives; neither delivers finite-sample support honesty plus pointwise efficient scalar adaptation for this six-endpoint map.
body.consumer: The result supplies a single prespecified report that remains honest in small trial cells without paying a permanent efficiency penalty on regular faces.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove the regular-face limit of the exact pilot-localized inversion and specify a simultaneous error calibration under which the claimed corresponding scalar side is asymptotically equivalent to the intended efficient Wald interval.
obligation.obstruction: Finite-sample honesty follows from exact nuisance-supremum inversion and error allocation, but the frozen primitives do not contain a uniform local conditional-multinomial quantile theorem or an inversion lemma. Moreover, the phrase 'the semiparametrically efficient Wald interval' does not specify whether its nominal error is the global \(\alpha\) or a simultaneous allocation; that distinction changes the limiting critical value when several sides are regular.
obligation.attempted: I completed the finite-sample construction with exact cell regions, conditional least-favorable multinomial quantiles, empty-arm logical ranges, and a Bonferroni allocation. A pointwise multinomial central-limit heuristic yields the efficient influence-function variance, but promoting it to the stated interval equivalence would silently assume the needed uniform quantile and inversion result.
obligation.partial_result:
The finite-sample coverage portion can be completed for the finite contrast lists.  Conditionally on pilot arm counts, form \(R_N\) by intersecting the three simplices with exact binomial confidence intervals for all \(3L\) cells, using total error \(\delta_N\); a union bound gives
\[
 P_p\{p\in R_N\}\ge1-\delta_N,
\]
including empty pilot arms by assigning their full simplices.  For a retained affine contrast \(\ell_r(p)\), main-sample arm counts \(m=(m_0,m_1,m_2)\), and error \(\eta_r\), define
\[
 c_r(t,R_N,\eta_r)=\inf\left\{c\ge0:
 \inf_{\substack{\widetilde p\in R_N\\ \ell_r(\widetilde p)=t}}
 P_{\widetilde p}\bigl(|\widehat\ell_r-t|\le c\mid m\bigr)
 \ge1-\eta_r\right\}.
\]
The conditional sample space is finite, the null slice is compact, and its probabilities are multinomial polynomials, so the displayed least-favorable quantile exists; an empty null slice is rejected.  If an arm needed by the contrast is empty, use the contrast's full simplex range.  Inverting these tests gives exact conditional contrast sets.  Allocate \(\sum_r\eta_r\le\alpha-\delta_N\), take closed interval hulls, and apply the finite maximum/minimum endpoint formulas.  On \(\{p\in R_N\}\), a union bound covers every retained contrast and hence all six endpoints with conditional probability at least \(1-\alpha+\delta_N\).  Adding pilot failure proves
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_L}P\{(\underline\theta_d(p),\overline\theta_d(p))_{d\in\mathcal D}
 \in\mathcal I_{N,1-\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha
\]
for every \(N\), with zero cells, ties, and empty arms retained.  What remains unproved is the simultaneous procedure's claimed scalar Wald equivalence under data-dependent localization.
